LESSON: INDICES AND LOGARITHMS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: CORE MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers and Algebra
Topic 1.2: Indices and Logarithms
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Indices and Logarithms, part of Numbers and Algebra in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 CORE MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: Why do we use indices and logarithms?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. express numbers in index form,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indices and Logarithms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. derive the laws of indices using factors,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indices and Logarithms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. apply the laws of indices in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indices and Logarithms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. relate index notation to logarithm notation to base 10

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indices and Logarithms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. determine common logarithms of numbers from mathematical tables and calculators,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indices and Logarithms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. apply common logarithms in multiplication, division,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indices and Logarithms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. express numbers in index form,

   Indices and Logarithms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. derive the laws of indices using factors,

   Indices and Logarithms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. apply the laws of indices in different situations,

   Indices and Logarithms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. relate index notation to logarithm notation to base 10

   Indices and Logarithms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. determine common logarithms of numbers from mathematical tables and calculators,

   Indices and Logarithms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. apply common logarithms in multiplication, division,

   Indices and Logarithms helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

G. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. write numbers in terms of bases and indices in purposive pairs or groups and share them with peers. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use appropriate assistive technology such as padded pens/pencils or be assisted by peers/learner support assistant,

2. discuss in purposive pairs or groups and generate the laws of indices. Those with speech difficulties could use augmentative and alternative communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application/ point/sign/write),

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. write numbers in terms of bases and indices in purposive pairs or groups and share them with peers. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use appropriate assistive technology such as padded pens/pencils or be assisted by peers/learner support assistant,
2. discuss in purposive pairs or groups and generate the laws of indices. Those with speech difficulties could use augmentative and alternative communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application/ point/sign/write),

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Indices and Logarithms together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: as the learner discusses in a group and generates the laws of indices.

● Digital literacy: as the learner reads and obtains common logarithms of numbers from tables and calculators.

Values:
● Responsibility: as the learner takes care of mathematical tables and calculators.

● Respect: as the learner appreciates the input of others while discussing in a group and relating powers of 10 to

common logarithms.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills - Self-awareness: as the learner discusses in a group and relates powers of 10 to common logarithms and

identifies the base.

Suggested Learning Resources

Number and operation cards, mathematical tables, charts on multiplication tables, writing materials made of heavy

gauge paper, multipurpose communication boards on numbers, white boards, slant boards, book holders, head

pointers, page turners, padded pen/pencil, adapted digital devices such as calculators and computers, projectors,

internet connectivity, positioning devices such as special seats with straps

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. express numbers in index form,
2. derive the laws of indices using factors,
3. apply the laws of indices in different situations,
4. relate index notation to logarithm notation to base 10
5. determine common logarithms of numbers from mathematical tables and calculators,
6. apply common logarithms in multiplication, division,

Remember the key question: Why do we use indices and logarithms?
